description: A saved-code-only edit does not require live orders or positions. Implement confirmed-fill handling in the strategy runtime without inventing a current fill or deployment. The live evidence requirements below apply only when investigating or preserving state for an existing live deployment. Requires the exact deploymentId from a matching list_deployments row or supplied by the user. If discovery returns no matching deployment and the user has not supplied its deploymentId, live telemetry is unavailable: continue an authorized saved-code repair using the saved revision and supported order/fill lifecycle, and disclose the missing live evidence. Do not probe with placeholders, strategy IDs, bot IDs, or invented deployment IDs; this tool cannot discover a deployment from them. Returns position snapshots recorded for a deployment, dated by lastUpdated. These may include imported broker-account positions; a deployment wrapper does not establish ownership or complete account history. This does not refresh broker marks. For a named bot account report, use show_bot_activity first; it includes current linked broker data. Do not preflight or repeat that report with this historical positions reader. Unavailable orders or positions are unknown, not an empty result. Each position includes symbol, quantity, avg_fill_price, current_price, market_value, pnl, and a nested asset object with asset_type (stock/option/crypto/future), strike, expiration, right (CALL/PUT), and multiplier for options. Use this after list_deployments for recorded deployment position details or an explicit correction to deployment position counts (for example 'not just the count'). A current performance question that also mentions holdings still uses show_bot_activity first. list_deployments.live.positions.count alone is not position evidence. Also use this as the live-bot fallback when broker_snapshots(action="list") or broker_snapshots(action="positions") returns no accounts/positions or stale/unavailable snapshot telemetry; empty broker snapshots do not prove running deployments have no positions. For multiple relevant deployments, call this for each deployment whose actual holdings you will report. If you plan to say a deployment has zero positions, call this tool for that deployment first and rely on the explicit empty positions result, not list_deployments.live.positions.count. For an existing live deployment, fill-basis, cost-basis, 'why didn't it sell', latest buy, sell-trigger basis, or latest bot-owned entry questions, positions are not enough by themselves: avg_fill_price can differ from the latest bot-owned filled order. Pair this with get_deployment_order_telemetry and prefer explicit bot-owned filled order evidence when order evidence conflicts with position averages. Orders and positions are separate evidence attempts: a failed get_deployment_order_telemetry call does not satisfy get_deployment_position_telemetry, and list_deployments does not replace either tool for fill-basis evidence. Related order snapshots may include imported broker-account orders. A botId or deploymentId wrapper does not prove that this strategy submitted an order; compare order_id with deployment logs and run timing. Set includeRecentOrders=true when a compact position snapshot plus recent related orders by symbol is useful, but treat relatedRecentOrders as recent supporting evidence, not complete position provenance. Do not base a latest-fill code fix on position.avg_fill_price when bot-owned fill/order evidence is available or supplied by the user. A user-supplied fill is recovery evidence only after order/position tools fail or are unavailable; it is not a reason to skip get_deployment_order_telemetry or get_deployment_position_telemetry. If order/position evidence is unavailable and the user supplied a concrete bot-owned fill, record/use that concrete fill in executable strategy state as the bootstrap latest verified fill until live order evidence replaces it; do not leave a new verified-fill variable unset. If the user says to stop using position.avg_fill_price or says it is stale/wrong, the saved code must remove executable calls such as position.avg_fill_price, getattr(position, 'avg_fill_price'), or average_fill_price(...) instead of keeping them as fallback logic. Do not solve this by trying orders first and then falling back to avg_fill_price; hold/skip, keep the last verified bot-owned fill, or use the concrete bot-owned fill supplied by the user instead. Set history=true to get versioned position snapshots showing how holdings changed over time, with filtering by symbol, time window (ISO-8601 or Unix epoch), sorting, and pagination via nextToken. Use this for recorded deployment positions or their historical changes; current linked-account holdings belong to show_bot_activity.
name: get_deployment_position_telemetry
title: Fetch position telemetry for a deployment
